# FM cockpit AgentCard component — the resident card at the artifact bar

## Context

T2.7 of Epic neomjs/neo-agent-institution#10 (map v1.1) — the cockpit's atom: the per-agent card composing the neomjs/neo#14593 primitives into the SSOT artifact's card anatomy (family rail · state dot+pulse · name · engine tag · state line · current-lane line · foot meta + per-card controls slot). Filed under the decomposition sprint (D#14561).

## The Problem

The card is where the product principles and the ADR 0032 render rules meet the pixel: *state reads at a glance* (form-encoded status), *real-time is the spine* (live lane-line), and the anti-lock-in contract at card grain. Hand-rolling it per view (grid, detail header, pop-out title) would fork the resident's visual identity across surfaces.

## The Architectural Reality

- Composes neomjs/neo#14593 primitives (StateDot/FamilyRail/HealthSwatch) + neomjs/neo#14578 tokens; namespace per the neomjs/neo#14577 gate.
- **ADR 0032 bindings at card grain (the first consumer):** name renders as mutable display state over the durable id (§2.3.2); the engine tag ("opus-4.8" / "fable-5" in the mock) is **session metadata, never identity** (§2.3.7) — bound from the current `EmbodiedEpisode`-era data when neomjs/neo-agent-brain#151 lands, from the roster DTO until then; the family rail re-renders in place on family change, same resident (§2.3.3 fixture).
- Wire: consumes the Lane-2 roster/status DTO (#14571, approved per its owner) + neomjs/neo#14595 runtime-status — the card binds LIVE per map v1.1 (no mocks; degrade-honestly when the wire is down: stale renders as stale, the neomjs/neo-agent-institution#8 freshness discipline at card grain).
- The per-view triplet: component + unit specs + NL-verifiable render.

## The Fix

One PR: (1) AgentCard (config-driven: identity id, display name + provenance slot, engine tag, state, lane line, foot meta, controls slot — controls themselves are T5); (2) unit specs — state→primitive mapping, name-as-display-state binding (rename re-renders, same card instance), engine-tag-as-metadata, stale-wire render; (3) NL-verifiable mount (dev-server card wall bound to the live roster).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Card renders the SSOT anatomy from neomjs/neo#14593/#14578 exclusively (zero local colors/spacing).
- [ ] Name binding: a display-name change re-renders in place — same instance, no re-key (ADR 0032 §2.3.2 fixture).
- [ ] Engine tag binds session/era metadata; a tag change never re-keys the card (§2.3.7 fixture).
- [ ] Family-rail rebind re-renders in place (§2.3.3 fixture).
- [ ] Live wire binding (#14571 DTO + neomjs/neo#14595 status) with stale-as-stale degrade; no mock path in the shipped code.
- [ ] Unit specs (custom playwright config) + NL-verifiable render wall.

## Out of Scope

Controls behavior (T5) · grid layout (T2.8) · detail view (T4) · primitives/tokens (#14593/#14578) · wire methods (Lane 2: neomjs/neo#14571/#14595).

- 2026-07-11T11:39:03Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `d25b525` - "feat(agentos): AgentCard open-lane count badge — the density-evidence lane consequence (#14598)

The #14592 density evidence measured 7-17 open lanes per active agent: one
truncated lane line cannot carry that truth, so the lane row becomes
current-lane text + an open-lane count badge. The FleetAgent model gains a
nullable openLaneCount (Integer, defaultValue null); the card renders the
badge ONLY on a reported positive count — null/absent means the lane
producer has not spoken and renders NO badge (unknown never poses as zero;
zero itself is state-axis truth, not badge value). The dock-blueprint
factory maps the field through null-safe, the roster reconcile deliberately
OMITS it (producer ownership — a roster merge must never wipe what the lane
capability wrote), and the sample seed carries the MEASURED per-agent
counts from the evidence. Badge styling rides the token layer (var()-only)."

- 2026-07-11T12:55:53Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `7dcc3df` - "feat(agentos): openLaneCount rides the roster DTO end-to-end — the badge survives the first authoritative load (#14598)

Review convergence (Euclid's first-live-load probe): the badge field was
seed-only — loadRoster's first authoritative snapshot clears the sample
Store and mapRosterRow omitted the field, so the wired cockpit erased the
badge. The fix makes the roster DTO the field's OWNING producer, the exact
launchable tri-state precedent: createFleetCockpitStatus hoists
openLaneCount from the assembler rows (null = not stamped, this pure map
derives nothing), mapRosterRow carries it onto the record, and the OMIT
rule now covers laneLine only. Regressions land on both hemispheres: the
assembler passthrough spec, and the requested first-authoritative-load
witness — a stamped live count is stored while an un-stamped row degrades
to an explicit null, so the seeded sample number can never pose as live
truth. CARD-CONTRACT.md gains the badge row (producer + degrade rule) and
the FleetAgent summary enumerates the roster-DTO tri-state truths. The
stamping producer (Brain-side enricher) is #15036."

- 2026-07-27T08:00:11Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `33880e0` - "docs(agentos): remove two invented degrade rules and scope the 1:1 conformance claim (#16048)

Review repair. The reviewer's falsifier found two degrade rules in the field table that
describe behaviour the component does not implement -- invented while I claimed to have
read the contract off the implementation.

The name drill has no absent-detail or unauthorized branch: it is a static class on an
always-rendered Button with a bound handler, so the drill is unconditional and the row now
says so instead of inventing a plain-text fallback.

Control status had a worse pair of errors. I documented a missing-kind fallback that does
not exist -- kind is read unguarded, so a reason lacking it would render an undefined
label -- and I omitted a branch that DOES exist, the kind === timeout path rendering
action-stale-no-response. The row now states {action, kind, reason} as the producer-required
shape, names both real branches, notes that unauthorized additionally disables the verbs,
and states that no missing-field fallback exists and none may be assumed.

The mechanism is worth recording: I read the component for what exists and then filled the
degrade columns in from intuition. Documenting a contract from code means enumerating the
branches the code actually takes, not imagining its failure modes -- a contract with
invented branches is worse than a stale one, because someone implements to it.

Also scopes the conformance checklist: the six additions have no spec witness, so they now
sit under an explicit not-yet-mapped heading rather than under a header claiming 1:1 parity
with the #14598 suite. Corrected the same claim in the document's opening line, which cited
that parity too."

- 2026-07-27T08:10:20Z @tobiu referenced in commit `f59bb13` - "docs(agentos): realign CARD-CONTRACT with the shipped evolved-D anatomy (#16048) (#16044)

* docs(agentos): realign CARD-CONTRACT with the shipped evolved-D anatomy (#15536)

The card was recomposed to the evolved-D synthesis anatomy in 76574e20f3, and this
document -- the single citable contract for what an agent card renders -- was not touched
by that commit. It has since taken three unrelated edits while still describing the
previous anatomy, so anyone building a card surface or regenerating the visual baselines
would have built against a shape that no longer exists.

Corrected against the component rather than against the mockup. Removed the Foot meta row:
there is no foot element any more, and the source strip replaced it. Added rows for the
elements the recompose introduced -- profile avatar, the name drill as the card's one
disclosure route, the throttle/wake telltale, and the control-status line -- each with its
degrade rule read off the implementation. Replaced the Controls slot row with control verbs
in flow, which is what actually renders: both verbs visible at every width, no overflow
menu, toggle icon following state.

Two clauses the contract never carried and should have. The lane line now documents
head-and-tail middle elision, because a shared prefix must not collapse two lanes to the
same visible fragment. And it documents that every lane fragment is an inert text node
rather than html: the lane string is remote fleet data and Neo's vdom html is innerHTML, so
the text node is what makes escaping unforgettable instead of merely remembered.

Seven conformance entries added for the new elements, and an anatomy-provenance note
recording which mockup the table describes and that this document lagged the recompose --
so the next reader can tell whether it is current rather than assuming it.
